name: Shunno

local_adaptation_notes: Shunno achieved a rare instance of a rock song becoming genuinely national civic property: 'Shoto Asha' (2009) became the official theme song for the 2011 Cricket World Cup, and 'Shono Mohajon' (from Bhaago, 2014), originally about oppression under dictatorship, was spontaneously adopted as the 'unofficial anthem' of the 2024 Student–People's uprising — demonstrating how alternative rock lyrics can be re-activated by listeners as protest material years after release, independent of the band's original framing.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (2007): formed by Imrul Karim Emil and Shaker Raza, quickly joined by Andrew Michael Gomez and Rafatul Bari Labib. Breakthrough period (2008–2009): debut album Notun Srot (2008) followed by Shoto Asha (2009), whose title track became the 2011 Cricket World Cup theme song — a major mainstream crossover moment. Consolidation period (2011–2017): Gorbo Bangladesh (2011), Bhaago (2014, featuring the politically resonant 'Shono Mohajon'), and Lottery (2017) sustained the band's popularity, with lineup expansion (Ishmamul Farhad, 2016) refreshing the sound.

listener_community_notes: Represents alternative rock's capacity for genuine mass-cultural crossover — via sport (Cricket World Cup anthem) and political movements (2024 uprising anthem) — giving the band's listener base an unusually broad, cross-demographic character extending well beyond a typical rock-fan niche.
